The generic name 'H5 Data Center' has also got it printed on the Sarpy County (Nebraska) and Bernalillo County (New Mexico) pages, where it does not belong. The Hillsborough County article, where it does belong, says the county has 'no data center application before it', which fits: this is an existing building in the city.

ft-1782858901235-6061.name: Calhoun data center (Highway 53)
ft-1782858901235-6061.why: The record's name was just 'Data Center', and that bare name has got this Calhoun, Georgia record printed on three Argentine pages (Argentina, Buenos Aires province, Santa Cruz province). The Times Free Press source describes it: 'an Atlanta-based developer is pursuing a 500,000-square-foot project that would cover 11 acres of a 57-acre tract off Highway 53 next to Fair's Auto Services & Repair'. Status 'proposed' stands.

ft-150.why: The Spalding County article says the county 'approved three data center campuses in seven months', and that 'By August 2026 the county had received nothing from any of the three related to a land disturbance permit'. The record's DCD source ('Application filed for 5 million sq ft ...') confirms Montana Property Group's Project Spalding was one of the two campuses 'approved last year by the Spalding County board of commissioners'. It is approved, and nothing is under construction.

ft-196.why: A capacity of 0 MW is a placeholder, not a measurement: the record cites no source at all, and the Bulloch County article does not mention this site. It should be blank.

ft-1783823589544-7821.name: Maquoketa data center (Jackson County)
ft-1783823589544-7821.address: Off Highway 61, industrial park south of Maquoketa, IA 52060
ft-1783823589544-7821.why: Both of the record's sources put the site 'on 46 acres off Highway 61, on land south of Maquoketa. Maquoketa is a city in Jackson County' (DCD), in the 'industrial park south of Maquoketa' near Walmart (Yahoo/local press). The record's address said Delmar, which is in Clinton County, so it is printed on the Clinton County page, whose article is about an unrelated QTS campus. Status 'proposed' stands (no developer named, 'few details').

ft-1782187388649-2944.why: The DuPage County article says 'In January 2026 the Naperville City Council voted 6-1 to reject Karis Critical's data center near Naperville and Warrenville roads ... capped at 36 megawatts'. It is rejected, not proposed. Also note: this Naperville record is printed on the Dubuque County, Iowa page, where it does not belong.

ft-1763572480079-2104.name: Prologis data center (Kosciusko County, near Leesburg)
ft-1763572480079-2104.why: The Kosciusko County article says 'The commissioners voted unanimously on April 22, 2025 to deny the rezoning', after an 8-0 plan commission recommendation to deny. That is 'blocked' (denied by a vote), not 'cancelled' by the developer, although Prologis afterwards said it would not pursue it. The bare name 'Prologis' has got this Indiana record printed on the Shelby County (Indiana) and Macomb County (Michigan) pages, which are about other Prologis projects.

ft-1784674300198-1510.why: The Johnson County article says 'DAMAC Digital, based in Dubai, wants to convert a warehouse at 31800 W. 196th Street into an $860 million data center ... On July 16 ... the council unanimously overrode the planning commission'. The record's DCD source is headlined 'DAMAC data center in Edgerton, Kansas to go ahead despite planning commission denial', so it is approved, not merely proposed. I used the article's address; the record's '32880 W 191st St' does not match it, and neither readable source gave an address. A residents' petition is still pending in court.

ft-291.why: The developer was blank. The record's source is DartPoints' own Louisiana location page, and the Caddo Parish page lists it as the DartPoints data center in Shreveport. Also note: this Shreveport record is printed on the Bartholomew County (Indiana) page, whose article is about a different DartPoints facility in Columbus, Indiana, and on the Buncombe County (North Carolina) page. It belongs on neither.

ft-1763326509042-3634.why: The Livingston County article says 'The developers of record are Stantec Consulting Michigan and Randee LLC', that Meta was named as the company behind it only by a township trustee ('Meta did not respond'), and that 'on the eve of a December 8 rezoning hearing, the Van Gilder family withdrew the request', with the treasurer saying it 'would resubmit once regulations were complete'. That is a withdrawn rezoning, not a cancelled project, and 'Stantec Consulting/Meta' presented an unconfirmed attribution as fact.

ft-1775149605384-7770.why: The Clay County article says 'In March 2026 the Liberty City Council approved $1.4 billion in bonds and $202.7 million in tax abatements ... for Metrobloks ... to build three data center buildings of about 568,800 square feet near Old Hughes Road', and 'What happens next: construction continues on both Google campuses, and on Metrobloks' Liberty site after its incentives were approved.' The developer was blank.

ft-322.why: The developer was blank; the record's own name is 'TierPoint - St Louis Olive Data Center'. Status operating is unchanged. Note that its only source is a First Alert 4 story about a proposed St. Louis moratorium, not about this building.

ft-1769472104271-6330.why: The Lee County article says 'A data center that was never formally proposed set off Lee County's argument', and 'No application was ever filed'. Deep River Data had only 'asked state officials about tapping natural gas from Butler Well No. 3'. That is an inquiry, not a proposal, and nothing reports it being pursued or dropped since. The first real Lee County application is a different project (PointOne/Helix/CyrusOne, 90 MW, off Lower Moncure Road).

ft-1764168366775-9968.why: The developer was blank. The Otsego County article names 'a startup called Eco-Yotta Inc.' as the applicant to rezone 357 County Highway 9. Status 'suspended' is left: the board 'tabled the application pending more information', and the town then adopted a 12-month moratorium in May 2026.

ft-1778088996829-8003.name: Waterville Township data center inquiry
ft-1778088996829-8003.why: 'Waterville Data Center Land Advertisement' is a research note, not a project name, and the page prints it. The record's Toledo Blade source is headlined that a company 'is interested' in Waterville Township. The Lucas County article says only that 'developers had already approached landowners' while the township adopted a one-year moratorium. No developer, site or application exists, which is why the name should say inquiry. Status 'proposed (early)' is left.

ft-1784230987783-1009.why: The Marion County article says Verrus 'decided to proceed' and 'the first-phase application Verrus filed on July 31 describes two buildings of about 600,000 square feet on about 100 acres'. The governor cancelled the sale of 32 state-owned acres, 'about half the site', and Verrus 'is looking at an adjacent 32-acre parcel'. The project has a live application and is not suspended. The article names Verrus ('a California company funded by Google') as the developer. The record's own DCD source calls it an 'Alphabet spin-out'; Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners is not named on the page.

ft-1773441380040-9264.developer: DEPG Mosier Associates LP / DEPG of Shawnee II LP
ft-1773441380040-9264.why: The Monroe County article says 'The developer, DEPG Mosier Associates LP and DEPG of Shawnee II LP, first showed the township planning commission a sketch plan', with DCD linking the plan to Legend Properties. 'Gateway Development' is not a name the article or source uses. Status 'proposed' is right: the conditional use application is filed, but its hearing is not yet scheduled.

ft-1785380999931-4842.developer: Slate Belt Holdings (Talen / River Pointe Logistics)
ft-1785380999931-4842.why: The developer was blank. The Northampton County article says 'in Upper Mount Bethel Township, Slate Belt Holdings, a partnership of Talen and the River Pointe Logistics team, bought about 754 acres of ... River Pointe Commerce Park' and 'plans a 23-building campus', matching the record's DCD source ('Talen looks to develop 23-building data center campus'). I left capacity blank: the article gives '480-megawatt substation and a possible 2 gigawatts', which are the substation and a ceiling.

ft-497.why: The Coffee County article says 'Then the base project collapsed. On June 1 Arnold AFB said the Air Force had been told that potential lessees would not submit proposals for its parcels.' No developer ever came forward and the offering drew no bids, so the site is not a live proposal. Whether the Air Force will offer the land again 'was not stated'.

ft-1784673433709-2419.developer: Google (filed via Planton Investments LLC / Platon Investments LLC)
ft-1784673433709-2419.why: The Wilbarger County article says 'Google said in February 2026 that it has a data center under construction in Wilbarger County', and that the state filings for Project Rise 1A and 2A show 'work starting March 31, 2026 and due to finish by the end of March 2028', filed by 'Planton Investments LLC and Platon Investments LLC, both giving Google's headquarters as their address'. The developer was blank and the status said proposed. (The article, and I, keep both LLC spellings as filed.)

ft-892.why: This is not a data center project. The record's source (Scott County's 'Sites & Buildings' page) describes the Scott County Regional Business & Technology Park as a 65-acre marketed industrial tract, 'designated as one of twelve Premier Data Center Sites in the TVA Region'. It is a site being advertised to prospects. No developer, application or proposal exists, and it appears on no built page.

ft-1784758454457-8638.why: The Petersburg article says 'NuVu Real Estate had site plan approval in February for a three-building, 300 megawatt, $1.1 billion campus on 75 acres at 2588 County Drive by Interstate 95'. That is approval of a site plan, not construction. The article reports no groundbreaking. It also gives the developer, capacity and street address, which the record lacked.

ft-1043.name: Austin Ridge Logistics Center
ft-1043.why: The name was misspelled 'Logisitics'. The record's Fredericksburg Free Press source spells it 'Austin Ridge Logistics Center' and says 'The applicant is Nathaniel Hagedorn of NP Austin Ridge LLC', proposing 'about 1.6 million square feet of data center buildings' on 183 acres at the end of Cedar Lane. The developer was blank. Status proposed is unchanged.

ft-1765226206392-3158.name: Atlas Agro data center (Richland)
ft-1765226206392-3158.why: The name 'Atlas Agro' was just the company name, and the developer was blank. The Benton County article says 'Atlas Agro North America, a Swiss startup ... added a $500 million data center complex next door' to its fertilizer plant, and holds 'a one-year option to buy nearly 275 city-owned acres at 2100 Horn Rapids Road'. Status 'proposed' is right: the city manager says the option 'is not a land sale, construction permit, or final project approval'.
